doc.title: Bayes' theorem
doc.sheet:
concept posterior: P(A|B)
  name after
  say how likely A is once you know B happened
  label below after
concept likelihood: P(B|A)
  name fit
  say how likely B is when A is true
  border
concept prior: P(A)
  name before
  say how likely A was before you knew about B
  label above before
concept evidence: P(B)
  name all of B
  say how likely B is, whether or not A is true
  label below
doc.prose: Start from how likely A was [before](prior), scale it by how well A [fits](likelihood) what you saw, and divide by how likely the evidence was [all told](evidence) to get the chance [after](posterior).

doc.title: The rendering equation
doc.formulas: L_o(x, \omega_o) = L_e(x, \omega_o) + \int_{\Omega} f_r(x, \omega_i, \omega_o) \, L_i(x, \omega_i) \, (\omega_i \cdot n) \, d\omega_i
doc.sheet:
concept outgoing: L_o(x, \omega_o)
  name light out
  say the light leaving point x towards the viewer
  label below light out
concept emitted: L_e(x, \omega_o)
  name glow
  say light the point gives off by itself
  label below glow
concept hemisphere: \int_{\Omega}
  name every direction
  say add up over the half sphere above the point
  pointer
concept bounce: f_r(x, \omega_i, \omega_o)
  name bounce chance
  say the share of light from one direction sent on to the viewer
  brace below bounce
concept incoming: L_i(x, \omega_i)
  name light in
  say light arriving from one direction
  border
concept angle: (\omega_i \cdot n)
  name tilt
  say light at a slant spreads out and counts for less
doc.prose: The [light out](outgoing) of a point is its own [glow](emitted), plus the [light in](incoming) from [every direction](hemisphere), each scaled by its [bounce chance](bounce) and its [tilt](angle). The light in comes from this same equation at other points.

doc.title: How fast momentum converges
doc.sheet:

  name condition number
  say how stretched the bowl is: steepest curve over flattest
concept steep: \lambda_n
  name steepest curve
  slider 1 .. 100 step 1 = 50
concept flat: \lambda_1
  name flattest curve
  slider 1 .. 10 step 1 = 1
concept steps: k
  scrub 0 .. 60 step 1 = 10

  name rate

  y from 0 to 1
  mark steps point k = k
doc.prose: The [condition number](condition) compares the [steepest](steep) and [flattest](flat) curves of the bowl. The closer it is to 1, the smaller the [rate](rate), and the faster the error shrinks over the [steps](steps).

doc.title: Exponential growth
doc.formulas:

doc.title: The Bellman equation

  label below

  brace below best next move
doc.prose: The [value](value) of a move is the [reward](reward) it brings now, plus the [best next move](future) after it, worth a little less by the [discount](discount).

concept miss: y_i - \hat{y}_i
  name miss
  say the true value take away the guess
  border
concept guess: \hat{y}_i
  name guess
  say what the model predicts for example i
  tint
doc.prose: The [error](loss) is the [average](average) of each [miss](miss) squared, so a [guess](guess) twice as far off costs four times as much.

doc.title: Period of a pendulum
doc.sheet:
concept length: L
  unit m
  slider 0.1 .. 3 step 0.1 = 1
  label above
concept gravity: g
  unit m/s²
  say the pull of gravity: 9.8 on Earth, 1.6 on the Moon
  slider 1 .. 25 step 0.1 = 9.8
concept period: T
  unit s
  say the time for one swing there and back
  label below
plot T over L from 0.1 to 3
  y from 0 to 4
  mark length point L = L
doc.prose: A longer [length](length) swings slower; stronger [gravity](gravity) swings faster. The [period](period) does not depend on how heavy the weight is.

doc.title: Distance under steady speeding up
doc.sheet:
concept start: u
  name starting speed
  unit m/s
  slider 0 .. 20 step 1 = 5
concept speedup: a
  name speeding up
  unit m/s²
  slider -10 .. 10 step 0.5 = 2
concept time: t
  unit s
  slider 0 .. 10 step 0.5 = 3
concept distance: s
  unit m
  label below
plot s over t from 0 to 10
  y from -20 to 160
  mark time point t = t
doc.prose: The [distance](distance) is what the [starting speed](start) covers plus what the [speeding up](speedup) adds, and that part grows with the square of the [time](time).
